title: Hold an interest in a pharmacy business only with an eligibility certificate
what: Only a pharmacist (or another person the Act allows) may own, or hold an interest in, a pharmacy business. In Tasmania a person needs an eligibility certificate, or must be an exempt person, to hold an interest.

sources.title: Pharmacy Control Act 2001 (Tas)
sources.quote: A person must not hold an interest in a pharmacy business unless – (a) the person holds an eligibility certificate; or (b) [Section 62 Subsection (1) amended by No. 22 of 2016, s. 16, Applied:01 Jan 2017] the person is an exempt person. Penalty: Fine not exceeding 200 penalty units and, in the case of a continuing offence, a further fine not exceeding 20 penalty units for each day during which the offence continues.

confidence_note: The Act's own words bar holding an interest in a pharmacy business without an eligibility certificate.

assessment.summary: Only pharmacists may own pharmacies, and each may own only a few. It keeps other investors and business models out of community pharmacy; the Harper Review recommended removing the restriction.

marks.reason: Reserves ownership of pharmacies to pharmacists and caps how many each may own: an exclusive right to enter.

assessment.confidence_note: The restriction is explicit; its effect on prices and access has not been measured in Australia. Marks copied from the register item tas-pharmacy-ownership so the two agree.
